Trustworthy Evaluation of AI-Assisted Painting Restoration

OpenCV Telea

Evaluation status: fully_evaluated. This report summarizes validated Notebook 09–30 evidence and creates no new scientific evidence.

Executive Summary

This standalone report evaluates OpenCV Telea using validated restoration, metric, robustness, uncertainty, failure, explanation, and compute evidence.

Evaluation statusfully_evaluatedComplete scope
Paintings50410 cases
Candidates410410 with explanation-catalog coverage
First-place anchors1/11core_three_model
Mean runtime0.453 sRecorded local system
Flagged candidates390/410At least one triggered trustworthiness flag
Thesis alignment: RQ1, RQ2, and RQ3: model quality, conditional behaviour, and support for human review.

What the evidence shows

  • Evaluation status: fully_evaluated.
  • Coverage: 50 paintings, 410 cases, and 410 candidates.
  • Observed mean runtime: 0.453 seconds per candidate on the recorded system.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea ranked second: it was worse overall than LaMa but better than Stable Diffusion under the approved family-balanced evaluation.
Limitation: Visual plausibility is not equivalent to historical or restoration trustworthiness. Unmeasured physical-conservation outcomes remain inconclusive.

1. Method Identity

This section defines what the evaluated method is, what role it can reasonably serve, and where that role ends.

Field Value
Model family Classical Fast Marching Inpainting
Methodological role Classical Deterministic Baseline
Implementation OpenCV cv2.INPAINT_TELEA
Model identifier cv2.INPAINT_TELEA
Deterministic True
Prompt dependent False
Execution device cpu
Precision uint8

Intended uses

  • classical deterministic restoration baseline
  • small local damage and thin-scratch comparison
  • reproducible candidate generation for controlled evaluation

Excluded uses

  • historically verified reconstruction
  • semantic reconstruction of large missing structures
  • conservation approval
Thesis alignment: RQ3: defines the model's appropriate role in a human-centred evaluation workflow.

What the evidence shows

  • Strengths: fast and deterministic; transparent classical baseline; low compute burden.
  • Weaknesses: no semantic understanding; limited large-mask reconstruction; local interpolation may lose meaningful structure.
  • Intended uses: classical deterministic restoration baseline; small local damage and thin-scratch comparison; reproducible candidate generation for controlled evaluation.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea is better treated as classical deterministic baseline than as an autonomous restoration authority.
Limitation: The evaluated implementation and configuration do not establish historically authentic recovery.

3. Overall Quality Evidence

Eleven transparent quality anchors combine classical, perceptual, feature, spatial, local, semantic, and structural evidence. Lower plotted rank is better.

Thesis alignment: RQ1: compares restoration quality using transparent complementary evidence.

What the evidence shows

  • The model ranked first on 1 of 11 transparent quality anchors in its approved comparison population.
  • Family-balanced baseline rank: 2 of three complete-scope methods.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea ranked second: it was worse overall than LaMa but better than Stable Diffusion under the approved family-balanced evaluation.
Limitation: Ranks summarize metric-defined behaviour; they do not prove historical correctness or universal model superiority.

4. Damage Types and Experiments

This section keeps damage-size sensitivity, mask robustness, and synthetic-degradation evidence separate. Positive adverse slopes indicate worse restoration behaviour under the stated exposure.

Thesis alignment: RQ2: tests whether behaviour changes with damage size, mask geometry, and synthetic degradation.

What the evidence shows

  • Damage-size deterioration was confirmed on 6 of 11 anchors.
  • 5 of 11 damage-size intervals crossed zero and remain inconclusive.
  • Synthetic-degradation severity produced 11 adverse and 22 opposite-direction metric-family summaries.
Conclusion: Larger damage made OpenCV Telea worse on 6 anchors with intervals entirely above zero. The remaining 5 anchors do not support a directional claim. Synthetic degradation was mixed rather than uniformly better or worse.
Limitation: Extension experiments contain five paintings for the core models. Metric-native slope sizes cannot be compared directly across different anchors.

5. Texture, Colour, and Seam Behaviour

Local texture, colour, and seam diagnostics test whether a plausible-looking repair remains visibly inconsistent near or inside the restored region.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and approved local-consistency extension: evaluates defects missed by global similarity.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place local anchors: 0 of three.
  • The three anchors cover local texture error, masked colour difference, and boundary-seam mismatch.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea was not best on any of the three local anchors and was worse than at least one comparator for texture, colour, and seam evidence.
Limitation: Each anchor measures a different failure mode; their numerical scales are not interchangeable.

6. Semantic and Structural Evidence

Semantic and structural measurements test local content and organization beyond pixel similarity. They remain proxies rather than proof of historical meaning.

Thesis alignment: RQ1 and the semantic/XAI extension: evaluates whether local structure and meaning are preserved.

What the evidence shows

  • First-place semantic or structural anchors: 1 of three.
  • The evidence covers local semantic DINO, structural affinity, and structural SSIM.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea was better on 1 of three semantic and structural anchors, producing a mixed result.
Limitation: Feature agreement does not establish iconographic correctness, artist intent, or historical truth.

7. Uncertainty, Prompt, and Stability Evidence

Uncertainty is treated as empirical repeated-seed variability only. Deterministic methods and insufficient seed coverage are reported as not applicable.

Thesis alignment: RQ2 and uncertainty extension: distinguishes stochastic sensitivity from restoration quality.

What the evidence shows

  • OpenCV Telea is deterministic under the evaluated contract.
  • Repeated-seed diffusion uncertainty is therefore not applicable.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea is better for exact repeatability than a stochastic generator, but this stability does not mean its restoration quality is better.
Limitation: Empirical variability is not calibrated confidence and does not measure historical correctness.

9. Difference and Explanation Maps

These panels pair restored outputs with available difference, uncertainty, semantic, texture, colour, seam, or boundary diagnostics. Bright or intense regions must be interpreted using each map's stated scale.

Thesis alignment: RQ3 and XAI extension: supports localized human review rather than opaque acceptance.

What the evidence shows

  • 16 diagnostic-map tiles are embedded beside representative cases.
  • Maps are drawn from validated spatial, local, uncertainty, and semantic manifests where applicable.
Conclusion: The maps are better than scalar metrics alone for locating where a restoration changed or failed. They do not establish why the generated content is historically correct.
Limitation: Map colour and intensity remain specific to each diagnostic definition and scale.

10. Failure Taxonomy and Trustworthiness Flags

Failure categories describe observed metric-defined patterns. Trustworthiness flags convert supported patterns into auditable review actions.

Recommendation Candidates
Do Not Rely Automatically 98
Specialist Review Required 278
Suitable For Preliminary Inspection 34
Thesis alignment: RQ3: turns multiple diagnostic failures into auditable human-review actions.

What the evidence shows

  • The trustworthiness catalog covers 410 candidates.
  • At least one flag was triggered for 390 candidates.
  • Critical flags affected 150 candidates; warning flags affected 387.
Conclusion: Triggered flags mean automated reliance would be worse than specialist review for the affected candidates. A flag is a screening signal, not a final conservation verdict.
Limitation: Some flag families are unavailable or only partially supported for particular candidates.

11. Compute and Scalability

Observed execution evidence and the transparent 300-painting projection are shown separately.

Evidence Population Runtime Status
Observed complete evaluated run 50 paintings / 410 candidates 3.09 minutes executed
300-painting canonical-primary projection 300 paintings / 1,500 candidates 10.44 minutes central estimate projection, not executed
Thesis alignment: Approved compute extension: evaluates practical deployment and scaling feasibility.

What the evidence shows

  • Observed mean runtime: 0.453 seconds per candidate.
  • Observed p95 runtime: 0.698 seconds.
  • Projected central runtime for 300 paintings under the canonical-primary design: 0.17 hours.
  • Projected report-owned restoration storage: 1034.4 MiB.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea was better for speed on the recorded system, with the lowest observed mean runtime of the four methods.
Limitation: Observed timings describe one workstation. The 300-painting runtime and storage values were not executed experiments.

12. Decision Support

Strengths

  • fast and deterministic
  • transparent classical baseline
  • low compute burden

Weaknesses

  • no semantic understanding
  • limited large-mask reconstruction
  • local interpolation may lose meaningful structure
Thesis alignment: RQ3: translates evidence into a bounded human-review recommendation.

What the evidence shows

  • Main strengths: fast and deterministic; transparent classical baseline; low compute burden.
  • Main weaknesses: no semantic understanding; limited large-mask reconstruction; local interpolation may lose meaningful structure.
Conclusion: OpenCV Telea is better used within its declared role and worse when extended to excluded uses. Its outputs require comparison with the clean reference, local diagnostics, flags, and expert judgement.
Limitation: The report supports prioritization and review; it does not authorize treatment of a physical artwork.

13. Limitations

The limitations below are retained from the canonical model card and evidence contract.

  • Runtime and memory observations describe one recorded local workstation and software environment.
  • The 300-painting values are transparent linear projections, not executed experiments.
  • Projected storage covers notebook-owned output artifacts and excludes model caches, environments, Git history, and downstream metric outputs.
  • SDXL has ten completed candidates nested within five paintings and cannot support a full-scope ranking.
  • LaMa per-case runtime includes transparent allocation from IOPaint batch wall-clock measurements.
  • Quality-anchor wins are descriptive validated Notebook 21 evidence, not a universal quality or conservation score.
  • OpenCV Telea is a local interpolation baseline and does not reconstruct historically verified content.
  • A fixed radius of 3 is used without per-case tuning.
  • Eligible synthetic-degradation cases are supplementary masked-removal diagnostics and must remain separate from missing-content claims.
  • Runtime measurements describe the recorded CPU environment and are not universal benchmarks.
Thesis alignment: RQ1–RQ3: defines what the evaluation does and does not establish.

What the evidence shows

  • Excluded uses: historically verified reconstruction; semantic reconstruction of large missing structures; conservation approval.
  • 10 persisted model and evaluation limitations are retained from the model card.
Conclusion: The evidence can identify comparatively better or worse metric-defined behaviour, while historical authenticity and physical conservation suitability remain inconclusive.
Limitation: Synthetic damage, digital references, model-domain gaps, and incomplete human evidence constrain every claim.
